newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, except for silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, except for silver.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Friday, with the exception of silver, in choppy trade, on moderate volumes, traders said.

"In the next couple of days, gold prices are expected to remain in the same general area in anticipation of next Tuesday's FOMC meeting in which the Federal Reserve will decide whether or not to raise interest rates," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.
"But this remains a technical market and nearby support at $350 could be tested," he added.
COMEX April gold ended up $1.30 at $353.10 an ounce, after trading a $351.80-354.80 range, on estimated gold futures volume of 50,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $352.60/10, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $352.80 and the New York close Thursday around $351.30/80.
The OTC options expiry in London failed to provide much direction, but COMEX call option buying in both gold and silver in the past two days has helped to improve the tone, traders said.

COMEX gold open interest fell a further 3,604 lots Thursday to 164,294 contracts, its lowest level since last September, while open interest in April gold was down to 44,409 lots, ahead of first notice day on March 31.

Analysts noted that gold is still struggling to rise back above its 55-day (quarterly) moving-average, while COMEX May silver, NYMEX April platinum and NYMEX June palladium are all still holding comfortably above their 55-day averages.
But good underlying physical gold demand, signs of a topping out in the US dollar, and weakness in US stocks and bonds this week are all providing some support for precious metals, traders said.
Earlier this week gold prices slipped back below $350 an ounce, after recovering to around $365 in the past month from a three-year low at $336.
COMEX May silver ended down 5.5 cents at $5.160 an ounce, after trading a $5.230-5.145 range.
COMEX silver open interest rose 2,163 lots to 93,069 contracts Thursday, but May silver is still seen trapped in a $5.100-5.300 range.
The spot gold/silver ratio edged higher to 68.59, after recovering from a 22-month low around 65.60 in mid-February.
NYMEX April platinum ended up 60 cents at $382.50 an ounce, while NYMEX June palladium gained $1.80 to close at $154.25 an ounce.

In news Friday, the head of the precious metals division of Russia's Finance Ministry, Victor Rybkin, said it was not clear when talks with Japan on renewing the annual palladium supply contract with Japan would begin, and it was not clear when deliveries would resume.
There have been no palladium shipments from Russia to Japan under the contract since December when talks on a contract renewal broke down.

Russia's state budget was signed by President Yeltsin at the end of February, but a resolution providing the administrative authority for a renewal of the supply contract has still not been signed by Prime Minister Chernomyrdin.
Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world palladium market and Japan accounts for about 40 percent of consumption.
